newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine will not ban grain exports in '97 - dep PM.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine will not ban grain exports in '97 - dep PM.

text.p: The Ukrainian government has ruled that traders will not be banned from exporting grain in 1997, Deputy Prime Minister Serhiy Tyhypko told a news conference on Thursday.
Traders and brokers say they are still hurting from a ban they accused the government of imposing last autumn to ensure state grain orders were filled during a bad harvest year.
The government has never formally admitted to issuing a ban, but several government officials have recently referred to restrictions placed on exports last year.
"You can say we forbade the forbidding of grain exports this year," Tyhypko said.
Ukraine has forecast a grain harvest of 35 million tonnes this year against last year's poor 25.4 million tonne harvest, which the government blamed on a drought at the start of the growing season.
